name: Data Darbar
assumptions: The dossier gives no heading; 80.4 degrees, the footprint long axis, is used with the entrance at +Y.
Deck 6 m above the street: estimated from the drone view of the two-storey north front; no published level.
Gallery roofs 5.5 m above the deck, scaled from one courtyard photo.
Minaret tips 44 m above ground, fitted from two photos using the 46.3 m spacing of the OSM minaret feet; the dossier has no published height.
Two minarets, following the JAABE paper and photos; Wikipedia's four is not followed.
Minaret cones use the dossier gold; photos show them pale, the JAABE paper says gold leaf.
Mosque scale taken from a person standing near the glazing in the head-on photo.
The shell roof behind the front arc is not visible in any photo; a low form lofted to the rear of the OSM hall is assumed.
Rear and side walls of the mosque hall are plain: no photo found.
Tomb plan 24 by 22 m and position from the JAABE master plan and the drone view; the plan is not to scale, and the tomb was moved a few metres west to stand clear of the south gallery.
The annex south of the south arm uses the OSM outline with its west edge pulled back to clear the tomb fence; its elevation is plain.
All four tomb sides are built like the photographed ones: two corner towers and five cusped arches.
Jali infill placed in alternate tomb bays; one close photo shows jali in some bays but the exact pattern is unknown.
Dome radius 3.2 m and finial height scaled from the tomb front photo.
Skylight and sunken-panel positions come from the JAABE master plan, checked against the drone view; sizes approximate.
North and east gallery fronts are not visible in the photos and are built like the south gallery; the 25 north and 11 east bay counts come from that bay width.
South gallery has 19 bays counted in the drone view; court side galleries nine bays each and cross arms estimated.
North and south gate pavilions take their plan from the OSM ring; their elevations are the plainest arch form, no photo found.
South and east street fronts are simplified to rows of blind arches; north front to two window rows.

East entrance inscriptions are a coarse texture of abstract brush strokes in the photographed colours and positions; they deliberately spell nothing, because a low-resolution copy of sacred text would be wrong.
Tomb signboards stay plain green with border lines; their verse is not modelled.
Iwan mosaic is a stylised blue and gold repeat, not the real pattern; the two spandrel roundels are placed from the head-on photo.
Skylight colour is sampled from the drone view; the fine grid on them is a guess, the lattice is too small to resolve in any photo.
Canvas blinds are put in all tomb arches as in the two front photos; other sides are unphotographed.
Minaret shafts are plain white: the grey bands of an earlier version had no photo support and were removed.
Flag on the entrance mast is plain green and white, without crescent and star; size scaled from the entrance photo.
Deck colour follows the drone view (near white); the dossier sample #878A8E is treated as a shaded reading.
Trees are simple stand-ins for the planting seen in the drone view.
Rooftop plant, the green street tarpaulins, security barriers and the reported 2026 expansion are left out.
